problem: The text says the exponential subthreshold line 'joins the square-law curve of Chapter 1.3' at VGS = Vth. The square-law expression gives ID = 0 at VGS = Vth, so the two curves cannot meet there. The exponential law holds only below Vth (roughly VGS a few tenths of a volt under Vth), the square law holds well above Vth, and the in-between region (moderate inversion) is described accurately by neither. As written, a student will believe both formulas give the same current at Vth.
fix: Replace with: 'The exponential law holds for VGS a few tenths of a volt below Vth. Above Vth the square law of Chapter 1.3 takes over. In the narrow moderate-inversion band around Vth neither formula is exact, so the real curve bends smoothly from exponential to square law instead of meeting at a point.'

problem: 'Shorter L and narrower W shift Vth through short-channel effects' lumps two different effects together. The narrow-width effect (Vth rising as W shrinks) is not a short-channel effect.
fix: Write: 'Shorter L shifts Vth through short-channel effects (Chapter 1.6) and narrower W shifts it through the narrow-width effect; both change Ioff.'

problem: 'The current flows into the drain' is ambiguous about direction. In an nMOS with low VGS and high VDS, band-to-band tunnelling in the gate-drain overlap sends tunnelled electrons to the drain and holes to the body; the conventional current therefore flows from the drain to the body (out of the drain terminal). A student may take the sentence as a direction statement and get the sign wrong.
fix: Write: 'Tunnelled electrons are collected by the drain and the holes go to the body, so the conventional GIDL current flows from the drain to the body. Either way, the drain terminal carries this extra current even when the channel is off.'

problem: 'The slope of that line is the subthreshold swing S' is imprecise. On the log-current plot the slope is decades per volt; S is its reciprocal, in mV per decade. The next sentence defines it correctly, but the first statement invites the wrong unit.
fix: Write: 'The inverse of that line's slope, expressed as a gate voltage, is the subthreshold swing S.'
